requirements.text: Keep everything the site already does and says: the same pages, content, design tokens, header, footer, training filter and contact form behavior.
The existing acceptance tests must keep passing.
Keep Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router; no new framework and no backend.
`npm run build` writes dist/index.html for / as a complete prerendered HTML file.
`npm run build` writes dist/services/index.html as a complete prerendered HTML file.
`npm run build` writes dist/training/index.html as a complete prerendered HTML file.
`npm run build` writes dist/about/index.html as a complete prerendered HTML file.
`npm run build` writes dist/contact/index.html as a complete prerendered HTML file.
`npm run build` writes dist/404.html from the "Page not found" page.
Each generated HTML file contains that page's full text (header, h1, content, footer) inside #root.
In the browser React hydrates the prerendered HTML with hydrateRoot instead of rendering into an empty root.
After hydration the training filter still works.
After hydration the Menu button still works.
After hydration the contact form still works.
Prerendering is done by a small prerender script using react-dom/server renderToString inside react-router's StaticRouter.
The prerender script runs after `vite build` as part of the build script.
Every page's HTML has its own <title> using the titles the site already uses (e.g. "Services | The Bayes Group").
The home page title is "The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI".
The 404 page title is "Page not found | The Bayes Group".
Every page has its own <meta name="description"> of one sentence about that page.
Every page has an og:title Open Graph tag.
Every page has an og:description Open Graph tag.
Every page has og:type "website".
Every page has og:site_name "The Bayes Group".
Every page has a <link rel="canonical"> to https://thebayesgroup.com plus the page's path.
Add public/favicon.svg containing the bell-curve mark from the wordmark in teal #1F8A8A.
The favicon is linked from every page.
Add public/robots.txt allowing everything.
public/robots.txt points to the sitemap.
Add public/sitemap.xml listing the five pages at https://thebayesgroup.com.
Home "How we work": at 1024px and wider the four steps sit in four columns.
Home "How we work": at 1024px and wider the steps are joined by a thin horizontal line behind the numbered circles.
Home "How we work": on phones the steps stack.
The class the "How we work" section uses is styled so the layout actually renders.
The footer shows the wordmark, "AI enablement, training and custom development.", the nav links and "© 2026 The Bayes Group".
The repeated tagline paragraph is removed from the footer.
The class used by pillar card titles has its own styling.
Pillar card titles match the course and service card titles: serif, with spacing between icon, title and text.
After moving to another page the window scrolls to the top.
After moving to another page keyboard focus moves to <main>.
A link with a hash (e.g. /services#training) scrolls to that section instead of the top.
Hash navigation leaves the section visible below the sticky header.
Scroll and focus handling does not run on the first page load.
Contact form fields have a grey border normally.
Contact form fields have a teal border on focus.
Contact form fields are red only when that field has an error.
"Required" is shown the same way on every required contact form field.
DEPLOYMENT.md is updated for a static host.
DEPLOYMENT.md states that the dist/ folder can be uploaded as it is.
DEPLOYMENT.md states that no rewrite rule is needed because every page is its own file.
DEPLOYMENT.md states that unknown addresses get 404.html.
